newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish prison guards on alert after bomb threat.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish prison guards on alert after bomb threat.

text.p: Prison officers in Northern Ireland were on special alert on Wednesday after a suspected Irish guerrrilla bomb warning.

Television and radio in the British-ruled province broadcast a police appeal for vigilance on Tuesday evening after a caller using an Irish Republican Army (IRA) identification code-word told a radio station a bomb had been placed in a prison officer's car.
The caller said a device had been planted under the car while it was parked outside a social club near the Maze prison at Lisburn, ten miles (16 km) south of Belfast.
The caller said the car was no longer at the club and added: "The device either failed to explode or fell off the vehicle..."
A search by British army bomb disposal experts drew a blank but police urged people who had been at the prison or the club to check their cars.

Security sources did not know whether the warning was genuine but said they would not take any chances following apparent tit-for-tat attacks by the IRA and its extremist pro-British Protestant guerrilla foes in Belfast last weekend.
On Sunday, suspected hardline Protestants wounded a well-known Irish republican who supports demands for the creation of an all-Ireland state ruled from Dublin.
"Loyalist" guerrilla commanders have refused to say whether the attack marked the end of a two-year truce in their struggle to safeguard rule from London.
The IRA, which ended a 17-month truce last February, killed several prison officers during a 27-year armed campaign against British rule. It frequently used lethal undercar booby-trap bombs.
The IRA has bombed targets on mainland Britain since February and two British military bases in Germany and Northern Ireland.

Sunday's bomb attack was thought to be a reprisal by Loyalists -- so-called because of their loyalty to Britain -- for the wounding of a police officer by IRA men inside a children's hospital last Friday.
